## Purpose

Modules in `apps/dashboard/src/lib/` are the typed boundary between the dashboard UI and the backend transport. `api-client.ts` is the single place that owns `fetch`/`EventSource` and exposes the generic `call()`/`subscribe()` primitives; `dashboard.ts` and `doctor.ts` build on top of it, each wrapping one or more backend commands in a small typed function plus the TypeScript interfaces that mirror the Rust DTOs. Neither `dashboard.ts` nor `doctor.ts` ever constructs a `fetch`/`EventSource` itself — both route every request through `call()` from `api-client.ts`, and the header comment of each file states which commands it wraps and what its fail-open contract is.

## Convention

Folder: apps/dashboard/src/lib/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 4

Wrapper functions are thin: `export function fetchX(repoPath: string, ...): Promise<XRow[]> { return call<XRow[]>("dashboard_x", { repoPath, ... }); }` — one line of logic, no branching, no local state. Arguments are named in camelCase (`repoPath`, `specName`) even though the backend receives snake_case; this mapping is a guard-level invariant and is never renamed. Every exported interface carries a doc comment noting which Rust struct it mirrors and its `serde` casing (`/** mirrors the Rust \`GitInfo\` struct (serde(rename_all = "snake_case")) */`), and status-shaped fields use a string-literal union (`"ok" | "warn" | "fail"`, `"active" | "completed" | "cancelled"`) rather than a free `string`. `doctor.ts` additionally shows the raw/normalise split for a boundary the backend cannot fully type: a `RawX` interface for what actually arrives, a public `X` interface with tightened unions, and a `normaliseX` function that folds any unrecognized string to a safe default (`"warn"`) instead of throwing.

## How to apply

A new lib wrapper file imports only `call`/`subscribe` from `@/lib/api-client` (never a bare `fetch`), exports one interface per DTO with a "mirrors the Rust struct" doc comment, and one function per backend command named `fetchX`/`dashboardX`/`setX` returning `Promise<T>` via `call<T>("command_name", { camelCaseArgs })`. If the command can fail without the app crashing (missing file, absent binary, empty dataset), document and preserve that fail-open contract explicitly, matching the empty-state-not-onError guard.

## Examples

Ref: apps/dashboard/src/lib/doctor.ts
```ts
function normaliseStatus(s: string): DoctorCheckStatus {
  return s === "ok" || s === "warn" || s === "fail" || s === "skip"
    ? s
    : "warn";
}

function normaliseOverall(s: string): DoctorOverall {
  return s === "ok" || s === "warn" || s === "fail" ? s : "warn";
}
```

Ref: apps/dashboard/src/lib/dashboard.ts
```ts
export type SpecBucket = "active" | "completed" | "cancelled";

export function fetchSpecs(repoPath: string): Promise<SpecRow[]> {
  return call<SpecRow[]>("dashboard_specs", { repoPath });
}
```
